title: Marawi court issues arrest order vs. Levito Baligod, others for cyber libel
summary: A Marawi Regional Trial Court (RTC) issued an arrest warrant against lawyer Levito Baligod and 18 others in connection to a cyber libel case, with a bail set at P30,000 each.

blocks.text: A Marawi Regional Trial Court (RTC) issued an arrest warrant against lawyer Levito Baligod and 18 others in connection to a cyber libel case, with a bail set at P30,000 each.
Baligod and other respondents were ordered to appear before presiding judge Samina Sampaco Macabando-Usman of Marawi RTC-Branch 8 over the charges lodged against them.
"The bail for the release of the accused in this case is fixed at P30,000.00 each for CYBER LIBEL," the warrant read.
The warrant was signed on November 26 at Marawi City, Lanao del Sur.

Baligod is the counsel for the 18 men who introduced themselves as bodyguards of former congressman and alleged flood control scam mastermind Zaldy Co. They had claimed to have delivered suitcases full of cash to several politicians and personalities upon Co's instructions.
Several of the respondents in the Marawi arrest warrant have also been named in previous news reports as the ex-bodyguards.

No individual was named as the complainant, as "The People of the Philippines" was indicated as the plaintiff. However, Lanao del Sur 1st District Representative Zia Alonto Adiong later issued a statement saying that he had filed a case against Baligod and the others.

"Napakadali po para sa iilan ang gumawa ng istorya online, ito po ang nag-udyok sa akin upang magsampa ng kasong cyber libel. Hindi po tama na basta-basta na lamang magparatang ng kasinungalingan laban sa kapuwa, lalo na kung ang layunin ay manira at magdulot ng kaguluhan sa isip ng publiko," Adiong said.

(It is so easy to fabricate a story online. This is what prompted me to file a cyber libel case. It is not right that they will just make accusations and lies against others, especially if the purpose is to smear the reputation of others and cause chaos in the mind of the public.)

Adiong said he supports free speech, but said there is a difference if the purpose is to besmirch someone. Libel and are is not part of legitimate forms of expression, Adiong asserted, as it is already outside of the law.
Several of the bodyguards have already recanted their statements.
GMA News Online has reached out to Baligod regarding the charges, but he has yet to respond as of posting time. — VDV, GMA News
